extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and translators of ancient Greek mathematics (readers of Archimedes)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for interpreting and translating Archimedes' Greek mathematical language: lexical choices, grammatical constructions, proof structure, and technical terms for operations, proportions, geometry, and mechanics. Useful to readers reconstructing the original sense and idiom of Archimedean exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of νοείσθω and passive conceptual imperatives for constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Let straight lines be conceived νοείσθωσαν... let the sphere be conceived to be cut νοείσθω ἡ σφαῖρα τετμημένη.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archimedes often uses passive conceptual imperatives (νοείσθω/νοείσθωσαν) to introduce constructions ('let X be conceived/let X be drawn'). The participle for 'drawn' may sometimes be omitted (e.g. ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ νοείσθω ἐπιφάνεια). Translate and render such passives as impersonal or passive infinitival constructions to preserve the methodological stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active forms and subjunctive for conditional constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: The active is used (rarely) with ἐὰν + subjunctive: ἐὰν τέμωμεν (if we cut), ἐὰν ἀγάγωμεν (if we draw), ἐὰν ἐκβαλῇς (if you produce).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where Archimedes uses ἐὰν + subjunctive or active participles, render as conditional active constructions in translation. Note he uses (1) ἐὰν + subjunctive, (2) participles to express possible/ultimate actions, and (3) first-person singular forms for explicit constructions ('I draw OM...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Genitive of passive participle used absolutely
rubrics_metrics.description: The genitive of the passive participle is used absolutely, e.g. εὑρεθέντος δή (it being supposed found), ἐγγραφέντος δή (the figure being inscribed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate such absolute genitive participles as background suppositions or circumstantial clauses (e.g. 'it being supposed found', 'the figure having been inscribed'). Preserve the absolute nuance in English to reflect Greek idiom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verbs for constructing or producing figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Verbs and phrases: ὁμοιώσαι (to make a figure similar), ὀργανικῶς λαβεῖν (to find experimentally), εἰς ἄνισα τέμνειν (to cut into unequal parts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain the technical force of construction verbs; where possible keep literal renderings ('make similar', 'cut into unequal parts') and note specialized senses (e.g. ὀργανικῶς for experimental/methodic finding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocabulary and constructions for addition
rubrics_metrics.description: To add: προστίθημι; passive often πρόσκειμαι; constructions followed by πρός (with acc.) or sometimes the dative. For 'added together' συντίθεσθαι; sums: συναμφότερος, σύγκειται ἐξ (equal to the sum of).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Render προστίθημι/πρόσκειμαι with 'add'/'be added', keep prepositional patterns (πρός + acc. or dative) in mind. Use English equivalents that distinguish 'added to' vs 'added together'; translate technical nouns like συναμφότερος as 'the sum of both'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocabulary and constructions for subtraction and difference
rubrics_metrics.description: To subtract: ἀφαιρεῖν; passive forms ἀφαιρεθέτων; common terms: κοινά (terms common to each side), remainder λοιπός, difference/excess ὑπεροχή (or ὑπερέχει/ὑπεροχά), opposite λείπεται (with gen.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep technical distinctions: 'subtract from' (ἀφαιρεῖν), denote common terms as 'common to both sides' (κοινά), translate λοιπός as 'remainder'. For 'excess' use 'excess by which ... exceeds ...' to reflect ὑπεροχή constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocabulary and constructions for multiplication
rubrics_metrics.description: To multiply: πολλαπλασιάζω; multiply one another πολλαπλασιαζειν ἀλλάλους; 'to multiply by' expressed by the dative; 'multiplied into' sometimes ἐπί (with acc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Render πολλαπλασιάζω as 'multiply' and respect the datival expression for multiplicand. For ἐπί + acc. denote the target reached by the multiplication ('into'/'by').

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocabulary and constructions for division
rubrics_metrics.description: To divide: διαιρεῖν; 'let it be divided into three equal parts' διῃρήσθω εἰς τρία ἴσα...; 'to be divisible by' μετρεῖσθαι ὑπό.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate διαιρεῖν as 'divide' and keep numerically explicit phrasing for partitioning; render μετρεῖσθαι ὑπό as 'be divisible by'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms and usages for ratio and proportion
rubrics_metrics.description: Ratio λόγος; proportional ἀνάλογον; proportion (word) δυνάμει/ἀναλογία; mean proportional μέση ἀνάλογον; two mean proportionals δύο μέσαι ἀνάλογον; antecedents τὰ ἡγούμενα, consequents τὰ ἑπόμενα; reciprocal οὗ ἀντιπέπονθα; compounded ratio λόγος συνημμένος/συγκείμενος.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain the technical terminology: render λόγος as 'ratio', ἀνάλογον as 'in proportion', and translate special terms (mean proportional, continued proportion). Preserve the roles 'antecedent'/'consequent' when translating proportional statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical operations on proportions (names and transformations)
rubrics_metrics.description: 1) ἐναλλάξ (alternately/permutańdo), 2) ἀνάπαλιν (reversely/invertendo), 3) σύνθεσις λόγου (composition/componendo), 4) διαίρεσις λόγου (division/dividendo), 5) ἀναστροφὴ λόγου (conversion), 6) δι ἴσον (ex aequali).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When explaining proportional manipulations preserve the Greek technical names alongside the standard Latin/modern algebraic terms (alternando, invertendo, componendo, dividendo, conversion, ex aequali) to make the intended algebraic inference clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressions for arithmetic multiples and adverbial multiplicatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiples: διπλάσιος, τριπλάσιος, τετραπλασία; adverbial forms: δὶς (twice), τρίς (thrice), τοσαυτάκις; 'the same number of times as...' τοσαυτάκις λαμβανομένας.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate διπλάσιος/τριπλάσιος as 'double', 'triple', and use adverbial 'twice', 'thrice' where appropriate. Be aware of constructions comparing multiplicities of different magnitudes (e.g. 'as many times as A is contained in B...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Names for submultiples and fractional naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submultiples: ordinal + μέρος (e.g. ἕβδομον μέρος), special half ἥμισυ; non-unit numerators expressed by ordinal + compound (δύο τριταμόρια); special improper fraction names ἡμιόλιος (one-and-a-half), ἐπίτριτος (one-and-a-third).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Render these fractional expressions preserving the combinatory structure (e.g. 'two-thirds' as 'two third-parts' or 'two tripartite parts') and keep special names ('one-and-a-half') when they occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms for measurement and (in)commensurability
rubrics_metrics.description: To measure μετρεῖν; common measure κοινὸν μέτρον; commensurable σύμμετρος; incommensurable ἀσύμμετρος.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep technical contrast between commensurable and incommensurable; translate κοινὸν μέτρον as 'common measure' and ἀσύμμετρος as 'incommensurable'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical vocabulary and equilibrium expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanics τὰ μηχανικά; weight βάρος; centre of gravity κέντρον τοῦ βάρους; lever ζυγός/ζύγιον; suspension κρεμάσθω; to be in equilibrium ἰσορροπεῖν; to balance ἰσορροπήσει/ἰσορροπεῖν ἀπό τινων μακέρων ἰσορροπεῖν.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate mechanical terms with standard English equivalents ('centre of gravity', 'lever'). Preserve locutions expressing equilibrium/balance and prepositional distance phrases indicating moments/arms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labels for theorems, problems, and directives
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem θεώρημα; problem πρόβλημα; direction/requirement ἐπίταγμα; 'it is required to prove' δεικτέον; 'I assert' λέγω/φαμὶ δή; 'it is required (to do)' δεῖ δή.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In rendering propositions, preserve the formal markers (theorem vs problem) and the conventional phrases that announce the task. Translate δεικτέον as 'it is required to prove' and δεῖ δή for problem statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis and synthesis structure in problems and proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis ἀνάλυσις and synthesis σύνθεσις are distinguished; synthesis often introduced by συντεθήσεται τὸ πρόβλημα οὕτως; parts of ἀναλύειν used similarly; analysis and synthesis may be given 'at the end' ἐπὶ τέλει ἀναλυθήσεταί τε καὶ συντεθήσεται.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve the two-stage proof method when translating: an analysis (breaking down to known results) and a synthesis (reassembling the construction). Retain formulaic introductions to each stage to reflect the classical method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept of διορισμός (determination of limits) in problems
rubrics_metrics.description: διορισμός indicates the determination of the limits within which a solution is possible; problems that are always solvable 'do not involve a διορισμός' οὐκ ἔχει διορισμόν.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate διορισμός as 'determination (of limits/conditions)' and mark whether a problem includes such a specification; it affects whether a problem asserts existence under conditions or universally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vocabulary for 'given' and 'hypothesis' constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Given: participles of δίδωμι (δοθείς, δεδομένος, διδόμενος), δεδόσθω κύκλος; 'given in position' θέσει. Hypotheses: ὑποτίθεμαι, ὑπόκειμαι; 'with the same suppositions' τῶν αὐτῶν ὑποκειμένων.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Render δοθείς/δεδομένος as 'given' and ὑποτίθεμαι/ὑπόκειμαι as 'suppose'/'be supposed'. Maintain the idiom 'given in position' where positional data is essential. Note variants (δοθεῖσα, προτεθὲν) and translate accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructions for citing previous hypotheses or steps (tense and complements)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an earlier hypothesis is quoted the past tense is used; after ὑπέκειτο different constructions occur: (1) adjective/participle (ἴσαι ὑπέκειντο), (2) infinitive (ὑπέκειτο μὴ τέμνειν), (3) noun phrase (τὸ ἐπίπεδον ὑπόκειται διὰ τοῦ κέντρον).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflect the past-tense retrospective reference in translation; follow the grammatical pattern used after ὑπέκειτο (adjective/infinitive/phrase) to mirror the original syntactic relation to the hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of idiomatic connective words for inference and reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Therefore δεῖλον/οὖν/τοίνυν (οὖν/τοίνυν weaker), since ἐπεί, because διότι; διά + accusative expresses the reason why, διά + genitive expresses the means by which a proposition is proved (διὰ τῆς κατασκευῆς).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish semantic force of discourse markers in translation: 'οὖν'/'τοίνυν' as discourse starters, 'διὰ' + acc. as 'because/on account of', and 'διὰ' + gen. as 'by means of/through'. This preserves rhetorical structure of arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phrases for transferring proofs/adaptation to analogous cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of ὁμοίως (similarly), ἐπὶ πάντων... (the same argument holds for all rectilinear figures inscribed...), μεταγαγεῖν τὸν ὅμοιον λόγον (to transfer the same argument).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Archimedes indicates transfer of an argument to other cases, translate with 'similarly'/'the same reasoning applies' and preserve the explicit scope (e.g., 'for all rectilinear figures inscribed in the segments in the recognised manner').

rubrics_metrics.name: Concluding formulae for proved or absurd statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions: δῆλον οὖν ἐστι (the proposition is therefore obvious/proved), φανερὸν οὖν ἐστιν, ὃ ἔδει δείξαι, ἔδει δὲ τοῦτο δείξα; absurdity: ὅπερ ἄτοπον, ἀδύνατον.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate these fixed formulas as conventional conclusion markers: 'Therefore it is manifest', 'which was to be shown', and render ὅπερ ἄτοπον / ἀδύνατον as 'which is absurd/impossible'. Preserve their role as logical signposts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction/side/concavity locutions and prepositional usage
rubrics_metrics.description: In the same direction ἐπὶ τὰ αὐτά; on the other direction ἐπὶ τὰ ἕτερα; concave in same direction ἐπὶ τὰ αὐτά κοίλη; on each side ἐφ᾽ ἑκάτερα; with dative or ἐφ᾽ a constructions when referring to directionality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep spatial prepositional distinctions clear in translation ('on the same side', 'on the other side', 'concave on the same side as...'). Translate ἐφ᾽ ἑκάτερα as 'on each side of ...' for geometric locality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventional use of the definite article for 'given' objects
rubrics_metrics.description: The Greeks habitually say 'every/the' rather than 'a/an' (e.g., πᾶσα πυραμὶς τρίτον μέρος ἐστὶ τοῦ πρίσματος τὸ...). They talk of 'the given area, the given ratio' rather than 'a given area'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In translation note this stylistic difference and consider rendering Greek definite article with 'the' in contexts where English might use 'a given'; preserve the assumed universality or specificity implied by the Greek article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumptions about minimality and comparisons of lines/surfaces/solids
rubrics_metrics.description: Assumptions: (1) Of all lines with same extremities the straight line is the least. (2) Of surfaces with same extremities the plane is the least. (3) If two concave lines/surfaces one included between the other and the straight line/plane is lesser. (4) Of unequal magnitudes the greater exceeds the less by a magnitude that added to itself can exceed any assigned magnitude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these as foundational geometric assumptions (axioms/definitions). Translate and present them as preliminary assumptions used in subsequent propositions; preserve comparative wording (least/lesser/greater/exceeds) as logical premises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of specific geometric solids and surfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: bent/terminated lines (καμπύλαι γραμμαὶ πεπερασμέναι), concave in same direction (for lines and surfaces), solid sector (cone cutting a sphere with apex at centre), solid rhombus (two cones with same base and apices on opposite sides with axes collinear).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Render these geometric definitions precisely, keeping the constructive character (e.g. 'solid sector = the figure bounded by the cone's surface and the portion of the sphere within it') and ensure definitions indicate positional relations (apex, base plane, axes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition structure: exposition (ἔκθεσις), statement of requirement, proof
rubrics_metrics.description: After the setting out (ἔκθεσις) follows a short statement of what is required: for theorems δεικτέον, for problems δεῖ δή. Archimedes uses analysis followed by synthesis; the synthesis often begins 'the synthesis of the problem will be as follows' συντεθήσεται τὸ πρόβλημα οὕτως.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When organizing translations or commentaries, mark these conventional sections explicitly and keep their phrasing conventional to show classical structure: exposition -> required statement -> proof (analysis then synthesis).
